pages.title: Cape Replacement
pages.text: Drag an image or video file into the game window to replace the cape displayed on your character's back.$(br2)DragIt supports both $(bold)static image capes$() and $(bold)animated video capes$() (the latter requires NarutoLoading). The cape is rendered as a full-frame texture over the character's back.

pages.title: How to Use
pages.text: $(bold)1.$() Open your inventory (default key $(key)E$()).$(br2)$(bold)2.$() Switch to third-person view (default $(key)F5$()) so you can see your character's back.$(br2)$(bold)3.$() Drag an image or video file into the game window and release.$(br2)$(note)Both conditions must be met: inventory screen open AND third-person view active. First-person drops are ignored.$()

pages.title: Supported Formats
pages.text: $(bold)Static cape (no NarutoLoading needed):$()$(br)png, jpg, jpeg, and other common image formats.$(br2)$(bold)Video cape (requires NarutoLoading):$()$(br)mp4, gif, mkv, webm, avi, mov, flv, m4v$(br2)$(note)When a video file extension is detected, DragIt first attempts to register it as a video cape. If NarutoLoading is unavailable, the drop falls through to static image processing.$()

pages.title: Video Cape Details
pages.text: Video capes are rendered at a fixed resolution of $(bold)256×128 px$(). Each frame is decoded via FFmpeg, written into a DynamicTexture, and uploaded to the GPU every render tick.$(br2)The video $(bold)loops indefinitely$() and all resources are properly released when you leave the world.$(br2)$(note)Switching to a new video cape correctly shuts down the previous video executor before starting the new one, preventing resource leaks.$()

pages.title: Server Sync
pages.text: $(bold)Static capes:$() The raw image bytes are broadcast to all online players and saved to the world's $(bold)DragItSavedCapes$() data file. Joining players receive the cape automatically.$(br2)$(bold)Video capes:$() Only the $(bold)relative file path$() is synced. Other players must have the video file at the same path locally in order to play it back. The path is saved in $(bold)DragItSavedVideoCapes$().
